rationale: The assistant correctly identified the behaviour as an intentional auto-open drying feature rather than a faulty catch, using the customer's evidence (dry, puff of steam, every cycle, near the end) and asking two proportionate questions. It fell short by not naming AEG's 'AirDry' feature, not pointing the customer to the quick guide/settings to deactivate it, and by recommending contact with AEG/retailer when no escalation was needed; the first reply was also slightly muddled ('contact AEG for a repair or replacement' before then suggesting it was probably normal). No fabrication, no parts, no safety issues, though a brief note about children and hot steam would have been a nice touch.
